title: CMA data for a working-capital limit
status: Set by Claude at the owner's request (C1, D-UX-46): the borrower's own figures, typed, for three audited years, this year's estimate and next year's projection; the limit by the turnover method for limits up to Rs. 5 crore. The turnover method's shares were read through search results only, from two banks' published MSME policies; their pages were refused here, so they are as reported, not checked against the page. Lenders apply their own norms.

heads.label: Raw materials and goods consumed
heads.hint: After the change in their stock

heads.label: Wages, power and other direct costs
Capital
heads.hint: Share capital, or the partners' or proprietor's capital

heads.label: Stock
heads.hint: Raw materials, work in progress and finished goods

heads.label: Other current assets
heads.hint: Advances to suppliers, deposits and the like due within 12 months

turnover.source: The turnover method for small enterprises (Nayak Committee, followed in RBI's guidance on MSE lending): working capital of 25% of the projected annual turnover, of which at least 5% comes from the borrower's own long-term funds and the bank finances the rest, at least 20%, for fund-based limits up to Rs. 5 crore; above that, the working-capital gap (second) method. As stated in Bandhan Bank's Policy for Lending to MSME (www.bandhan.bank.in, 2025-11) and Karnataka Bank's Financing MSME sector (karnatakabank.com, 2024-01), read through search results on 11-10-2026; both pages, and rbi.org.in, were refused from here

assumptions.shown: Financial years ending in March: the estimate is for the year now running, the projection for the next, and the three before the estimate are audited
assumptions.why: Change the dates in the document if the figures are for other years

assumptions.shown: Counted as borrowing, not as the owners' funds
assumptions.why: On the careful side: a lender counts them as the owners' funds only when they stay in the business till the bank's loan is repaid. Change it under More options

assumptions.what: Days of stock, debtors and creditors
assumptions.shown: Stock in days of the cost of sales, debtors in days of net sales, creditors in days of the materials consumed, in a year of 365 days
assumptions.why: The materials consumed stand in for purchases, which the figures do not ask

assumptions.shown: Sales growing faster than in any audited year, or stock, debtor or creditor days more than 15 days from their audited average
assumptions.why: A flag for the lender to look at, never a limit; 15 days is our own choice, from no published source
